citation.authors: Leone A, De Amicis R, Bertoli S, Spadafranca A, De Carlo G, Battezzati A
citation.title: Absence of a sexual dimorphism in postprandial glucose metabolism after administration of a balanced mixed meal in healthy young volunteers

population.description: 18 women and 18 men, healthy normal-weight non-smoking University of Milan students (enrolment 18-35 y), screened to exclude fasting glucose >= 100 mg/dl and HOMA > 2.5, no oral contraceptives, women studied in the follicular phase; age and BMI mean and SD from Table 2 (total and by sex).

protocols.name: women_fasting
protocols.description: Women (n = 18): the fasting baseline sample, drawn after arrival at 08:30 and catheter placement, before the test meal; entered as a 30 min fasted run-in from 08:00 ending at the sample, 10 h of overnight fast by 08:30 (clock, run-in and fast length assumed)

protocols.name: men_fasting
protocols.description: Men (n = 18): the fasting baseline sample, drawn after arrival at 08:30 and catheter placement, before the test meal; entered as a 30 min fasted run-in from 08:00 ending at the sample, 10 h of overnight fast by 08:30 (clock, run-in and fast length assumed)

protocols.name: women_meal
protocols.description: Women (n = 18): balanced mixed meal (white-bread sandwich with ham, extra virgin olive oil and tomato) eaten within 15 min after an overnight fast, arrival at the lab 08:30; each meal was sized to 40% of the person's estimated daily energy expenditure, and the arm uses the group's mean meal as printed in Table 1 (866 kcal, carbohydrate 134 g, protein 35 g, lipids 25 g); venous samples 0-180 min

protocols.name: men_meal
protocols.description: Men (n = 18): balanced mixed meal (white-bread sandwich with ham, extra virgin olive oil and tomato) eaten within 15 min after an overnight fast, arrival at the lab 08:30; each meal was sized to 40% of the person's estimated daily energy expenditure, and the arm uses the group's mean meal as printed in Table 1 (1078 kcal, carbohydrate 167 g, protein 42 g, lipids 31 g); venous samples 0-180 min

left_out.what: all insulin concentrations: fasting insulin and insulin max peak by sex (Table 4), fasting insulin by sex (Results text), the insulin columns of the mixed model (Table 3: change from baseline at each time, sex and interaction terms, constant): printed in 'U/l', which read as printed is a fasting insulin of about 6600 µU/mL; the paper's unit cannot be corrected here

glucose, insulin and C-peptide AUC (0-180 min) by sex (Table 4): no unit or time unit printed and no rule (total or incremental) stated; the glucose AUC (10718 in women) is below the fasting level times 180 min (about 14900), so it cannot be a total area either
C-peptide fasting, time to peak, max peak and AUC (Table 4), changes from baseline (Table 3), Results text
body fat percentage by sex (Table 2, skinfold estimate): a percentage, and the paper prints no body weight to turn it into the model's fat mass in kg

glucose 'Time' coefficients of the mixed model (Table 3), i.e. the women's (and, with 'Male # Time', the men's) change from baseline at each time: the 95% CIs are model-based (patient random intercept, residual variance pooled over both sexes and all nine times; the same width at every time point), not the change's own between-person spread in the arm, which the paper does not print

glucose 'Sex (Men)' and 'Male # Time' coefficients (Table 3): differences between the sexes in the baseline and in the change from baseline, not a statistic the format has (men-minus-women of a change)
absolute glucose, insulin and C-peptide time courses by sex (Fig. 1) and their percentage changes from baseline (Fig. 2)
